title: Range Profile
conditions: Basic fuel 84 US gal, weight 3600 lb at start, gear and flaps retracted, mixture best economy cruise. No allowance for wind or navigation errors beyond the 45-minute reserve already baked into the chart.

verification.note: Re-measured pixel-by-pixel against reference/fig5-13-range-profile.png on 2026-10-01 (BASIC FUEL 84 gal solid curves only -- the TIP TANK FUEL dashed curves on the same chart were ignored, out of scope). Like fig 5-12, not all curves reach 16000 ft -- each terminates where the aircraft can no longer sustain that %power (full-throttle limit).

45.note: Terminates essentially exactly at 16000 ft -- matches the schema point, no extrapolation.

55.note: Same -- terminates essentially exactly at 16000 ft.

65.note: Terminates at 12000 ft. The at16000 value above (956) is extrapolated ~4000 ft past the real curve on its measured slope.

75.note: Terminates at 8000 ft. The at16000 value above (880) is extrapolated a full 8000 ft past the real curve -- same caveat as fig 5-12's 75% TAS curve.

verification.correctionVsOriginal: The original seaLevel values for 55/65/75% (930/870/700) were reasonably close to re-measured (961/928/868) except 75%, which was off by a large margin (700 vs. the measured ~868 -- a ~24% error, re-confirmed by three independent pixel reads at different rows). The 45% value was also revised slightly (970 -> 997). All four curves' relative ordering (45 > 55 > 65 > 75, i.e. lower power = longer range) was already correct in the original data and remains so.

confidence.75: high for the measured 868/874 points; low confidence on the at16000=880 extrapolation since it's 8000 ft beyond real data
